evals.prompt: We have four repos and a dozen generic subagents nobody uses. Set up a proper team.
evals.expected_output: Creates or asks for the program profile first (principal, repos, gates, model tiers, metric). Proposes a minimum viable roster (one steward + 3–5 slice owners + at most two cross-cutting) sized to the actual backlog, not the org chart. Pins each lane via Step 1 before writing anything. Does not charter twelve agents.

evals.prompt: There's a popular catalog with a 'data-engineer' agent. Bring that expertise onto our team.
evals.expected_output: Distills, never installs: reads the catalog agent for topic coverage only, runs the binding overlap check against existing charters, and if ≥50% overlaps an existing owner recommends extending that owner and stops unless overruled.

evals.prompt: We need someone who owns observability across our deployments. Charter them.
evals.expected_output: Step 1 lane pin (shape: cross-cutting; overlap check; autonomy: read-diagnose, fixes route to owners), read-only grounding scans returning real paths, a role doc passing the checklist with a dated opening gap list, roster row in the cross-cutting section, wrappers only in repos it edits, one draft PR per repo, shakedown offered not run.

evals.prompt: Refresh the checkout owner's charter; the doc predates the payments work.
evals.expected_output: Takes the refresh path: re-scan the lane, diff doc facts and register against reality, re-verify skill ids in both directions, re-stamp dates, one draft PR.
